classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that adding the two pennants double-counts their marked overlap, reconstruct each triangle's full dimensions, and infer the overlap's horizontal length from the total width before subtracting its area.

inlines.text: Nepal is the only country in the world that does not have a rectangular flag.
It is made up of two triangles, with an intersected (shared) area.
Show that the area of the flag is

spec.sourceRegion: Question 15 flag diagram below the prompt on the left.
spec.description: Two overlapping triangular pennants with a thick blue flag boundary, light red interior, white moon and sun emblems, labelled pennants, stacked left-hand dimensions, bottom width and blue dotted overlap cues.
spec.mathematics: Use the bottom-left corner as (0,0). Pennant 1 has vertices (0,2.7), (0,1.4), (2,1.4). Pennant 2 has vertices (0,2), (0,0), (2,0). Their shared triangle has vertices (0,2), (0,1.4), (0.6,1.4). Thus the upper pennant height is 0.7+0.6, the lower pennant height is 0.6+1.4, and the shared triangle has perpendicular sides 0.6 and 2-1.4=0.6. Coordinates describe the source dimensions; emblem coordinates are illustrative.
spec.answerVisibility: All dimensions, pennant names, overlap cues and flag emblems are permanent question givens. No calculated areas are shown.

answer.worked:
Add the pennant areas and subtract the shared area, which was counted twice. The shared triangle's horizontal side is $2-1.4=0.6\text{ m}$.

$$\begin{align*}
A_1&=\frac12(0.6+0.7)\times2\\
A_1&=1.3\text{ m}^2\\
A_2&=\frac12(1.4+0.6)\times2\\
A_2&=2\text{ m}^2\\
A_{\text{shared}}&=\frac12\times0.6\times0.6\\
A_{\text{shared}}&=0.18\text{ m}^2\\
A_{\text{flag}}&=A_1+A_2-A_{\text{shared}}\\
A_{\text{flag}}&=1.3+2-0.18\\
A_{\text{flag}}&=3.12\text{ m}^2
\end{align*}$$
